messages:
IncidentBot: PAGE — smart-routing anomalies detected for customer 'AcmePay' (prod). Spike in 5xxs and routing loop indications between eu-west and us-east. Please follow incident runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/policies/smart-routing

Mike (oncall): ACK. I'm looking now.

Sara: seeing repeated 502/504s in eu-west hitting variant 'gpt-7b-q4' — but traffic should be routed to 'gpt-7b-q2' for that tenant. Fallbacks are kicking and causing cross-region retries.

Miguel: quick check in the router: a lot of decision logs missing "policy_id" and "fallback_sequence" tags. makes it impossible to see which policy applied.

Anna: I'm not seeing decision logs for ~60% of the failed requests in that window. Are we sampling them out?

Nina: PD page came in from monitoring at 10:21UTC, ticket01824. Customer reported latency spikes + errors.

Alex: initial hypothesis: policy config drift — fallback_priority for eu-west was replaced with an older variant id that doesn't exist in eu-west pool, so router sends to us-east and then retries back.

Emily: CS reporting affected customers: AcmePay (prod), BetaShop (staging). Need impact summary for execs — 10:20–10:35UTC window.

Mike (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) disable cross-region fallback for eu-west temporarily, 2) pin AcmePay to primary eu-west variant, 3) reduce retry count at router from 3 -> 1. Applying changes now.

Miguel: pushing policy patch to admin API. curl command I'm using:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/policies/patch 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"scope":"acmepay:prod","patch":{"fallbacks_enabled":false,"pin_variant":"gpt-7b-q2"}}'
```

Anna: Patch applied, but decision logs still missing the policy_id key for many requests. Router binary isn't emitting route_context tags to the decision-logs Kafka topic.

SupportBot: Noted affected customers and created support tickets: ACME-4532, BETA-211.

Nina: After disabling cross-region fallback and pinning, error rate in eu-west dropped from 18% -> 2% within 3 minutes. CPU on frontend routers normalized.

Alex: We should also add a guard in the control plane deploy that validates variant IDs per-region. This prevents mismatched variant IDs ending up in live policies.

Miguel: found the config drift — last night's policy rollout (PR #4721) overwrote eu-west mapping; the variant id in the diff matched an old QC naming scheme. Looks like CI didn't validate region->variant mappings.

Anna: I'll open infra task to restore the route_context emission and backfill missing decision logs to a separate auditing topic: infra#948.

Mike (oncall): Handing off to Sara — I'll be available for followup but need to start recovery tasks elsewhere. Sara will lead post-incident.

Sara: taking over. Action items: collect router metrics/traces for 10:15–10:40UTC, correlate any cross-region sockets, and draft timeline. If decision logs are missing we'll rely on trace sampling and router metrics.

Emily: I'll draft a short customer-facing message: apologize, note mitigation and that we're investigating root cause. Will share for review in 15m.

Miguel: proposed long-term fixes: 1) enforce CI check for per-region variant mapping; 2) emit X-Routing-Policy and X-Fallback-Run headers for every request; 3) add alert when >5% of requests in a window lack policy_id in decision logs.

Anna: created tickets: infra#948 (route tags), infra#949 (backfill decision logs), infra#950 (alert missing policy tags). Assigning to Miguel/Nina.

Nina: Verified temporary mitigation is holding. No new Pages for 12m. Monitoring will keep a closer watch for 2hrs.

Mike (oncall): Closing page for now — severity dropped to P3. Please update the runbook with the need to validate variant IDs and add decision-log presence checks. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident status changed to RESOLVED (P3). Please complete postmortem: https://incidents.redwood/1782034567

Sara: Will own the postmortem and timeline. Key gaps to capture: missing route tags, absent policy_id in decision logs, and config-drift path in control-plane rollout.

Emily: I'll prepare customer note and share once the timeline is ready.

Miguel: final note — we should consider a small change to the routing default behavior: prefer fail-closed for tenant-specific model pinning to avoid cross-region waterfall for tenancy-sensitive traffic.

Anna: Agreed. We'll include that in the postmortem action items.

Sara: Thanks everyone. Adding :eyes: reaction to any outstanding PRs.

SupportBot: Tickets updated: ACME-4532 -> awaiting customer-facing note; infra tasks linked.

Mike (oncall): Good job team. Handing off fully.
